name: AccessiWeb Widget
author: Emanuele

sections.description:
AccessiWeb Widget adds an accessibility panel to your WordPress site. It is designed to help visitors customize the browsing and reading experience according to their needs, including people with visual, hearing, motor or cognitive disabilities.

The widget can support accessibility improvement work related to major standards and regulations, including:

  • WCAG 2.1 guidelines, level AA
  • Italian Law 4/2004 and AGID guidelines
  • Directive (EU) 2016/2102 and Directive (EU) 2019/882, European Accessibility Act
  • UNI EN 301549 technical standard

With AccessiWeb Widget you can provide:

  • 8 navigation profiles for different accessibility needs;
  • 10 content adjustments for readability and visual comfort;
  • 12 accessibility settings for perception, vision, hearing and navigation support;
  • 15 color adjustments for contrast, readability and visual comfort.

The goal is to make the website more inclusive and easier to use without changing the existing layout.

External Service

This plugin uses an external service provided by AccessiWeb to load and initialize the accessibility widget on your website. The widget is hosted on AccessiWeb servers and is loaded dynamically when a visitor opens a page where the plugin is active.

External service information:
* Service: AccessiWeb Widget
* Service provider: dunp scpl
* Terms of service: www.accessiweb.it/termini-e-condizioni
* Privacy policy: www.accessiweb.it/privacy-policy
* Cookie policy: www.accessiweb.it/cookie-policy
* UNI/PdR 125:2022 information: www.accessiweb.it/parita-di-genere

The plugin does not collect personal data from website visitors. The only recorded information is the number of pageviews, which is anonymous and not associated with identifiable data.

Features

Accessibility profiles

Eight navigation profiles help visitors adapt reading, navigation and interaction to different accessibility needs.

Content settings

Content settings allow visitors to change text size, spacing, line height and scale, highlight titles and links, manage images and adjust text alignment.

Accessibility settings

The widget provides tools for reading support, focus, keyboard navigation, cursor visibility, text-to-speech and other features useful for visual, cognitive or motor limitations.

Color settings

Color settings include monochrome mode, inverted colors, dark mode, saturation, brightness, contrast, blue light filter and text or background tint adjustments.

WordPress customization

From the WordPress admin panel you can configure:

  • License Key;
  • primary color;
  • horizontal and vertical position;
  • offsets and measurement units;
  • icon size;
  • icon shape: round, square, rounded;
  • icon radius for the rounded shape;
  • accessibility statement link and opening target;
  • custom CSS trigger;
  • custom keyboard shortcut;
  • option to hide the default button;
  • delayed widget initialization after the page has fully loaded.

White Label – Widget Large plan

With the Widget Large plan, the widget can apply white label parameters:

  • panel title;
  • accessibility button label;
  • custom information text;
  • footer text;
  • footer link.

These fields can be saved in the plugin settings, but they are applied by the widget only when the license returns the Widget Large plan.

Supported Languages

  • Italiano
  • English
  • Espanol
  • Deutsch
  • Francais

Pageviews Info

Pageviews are counted every time a page on your website is viewed and the AccessiWeb Widget is loaded.

Each view is recorded as a single pageview. This count helps measure widget usage and verify that it is aligned with the selected subscription plan.

The pageview counter is automatically reset on the first day of each month.

Privacy Policy

AccessiWeb Widget is designed with attention to privacy and compliance with applicable personal data protection rules, including the GDPR. The widget does not track or collect personal data from website visitors, including IP addresses.

The only data recorded in relation to the widget is the incremental pageview count, used only to measure how often the widget is served. This information is collected anonymously and is not associated with any data that can identify visitors.
